title: Indrajit's death
hook: Indrajit kills Sita in front of Hanuman, or seems to

segments.voice: Yesterday: the Hanuman Chalisa, and how two herb flights became one picture on shrine walls. The one who brings healing.

Indrajit rides out of Lanka's western gate with a woman in his chariot. She's thin, in a soiled garment, weeping, calling Rama's name. Hanuman sees her and freezes. He sat in the tree above her in the ashoka grove; he knows that face. It's Sita. In front of the whole monkey army, Indrajit seizes her by the hair, draws his sword, and cuts her down. Then he shouts across the field: there's nothing left to fight for now.
screen: `A WOMAN IN THE CHARIOT.` → `HANUMAN FREEZES.` → `NOTHING LEFT TO FIGHT FOR.`

segments.voice: Hanuman, who crossed the sea to find her, pulls the army back in despair and goes to tell Rama. Rama, hearing it, collapses. Lakshmana holds him and, in grief, rails against a world where doing right seems to bring only suffering. Then Vibhishana arrives, the one person in the camp who knows how Lanka thinks. That wasn't Sita, he says. Ravana would never allow her to be killed; he wants her too much. It was an illusion, a magic double, and a distraction. Right now Indrajit is on his way to Nikumbhila, a sacred grove and shrine, to complete a fire offering. If he finishes it, he'll be unbeatable. But Brahma's boon has a condition: whoever attacks him there, before the rite is done, can kill him. So send Lakshmana now. Look at what Indrajit has done. He didn't need to win a battle. He needed a few hours, and he knew exactly what would stop his enemies cold: the sight of the person they love most, dying. It's a cruel weapon, because it doesn't touch the body. It goes straight for the heart, and for a while it works. What breaks the spell isn't strength. It's a calm voice that knows the enemy, saying: look again; this isn't what it seems. Rama, steadied, sends Lakshmana off with Vibhishana, Hanuman and an army. The race to Nikumbhila begins.
screen: `RAMA COLLAPSES.` · `VIBHISHANA: IT WAS AN ILLUSION.` · `THE FIRE AT NIKUMBHILA.` · `A WEAPON AIMED AT THE HEART.` · then, large: `LOOK AGAIN; IT ISN'T WHAT IT SEEMS.`

segments.voice: Picture a fear that has gripped you lately, a scene your mind showed you of something terrible happening. Breathe slowly, and with each breath ask, in Vibhishana's calm voice, what you actually know, until the picture loosens its hold a little.
Indrajit's death. It begins with his cruelest trick, a magic Sita cut down before the army, and Vibhishana seeing through it to the fire at Nikumbhila.
Your line: it isn't what it seems. The race reaches the grove next. Day six hundred fifty-two.

howItsDone: Some Ramayana tellers use the illusory Sita, the māyā-sītā of this episode, to talk about māyā, illusion, and how fear can make what is false look real.

original.note: Sanskrit māyā: magic power or illusion; Indrajit's double of Sita is called māyā-sītā, the illusory Sita.

trapdoor: what you thought: Indrajit was just a strong warrior.
what it means: his worst weapon here is an illusion aimed at the heart, to buy time for his rite.
what a scholar hears: Vibhishana reveals Brahma's condition: whoever strikes Indrajit at Nikumbhila before the rite is done can kill him.

chat.says: Did Indrajit really kill Sita in front of the whole army?
options: No. It was a magic double, meant to stop them while he finished his fire rite.
Yes, but the gods brought her back to life before Rama could hear.
No. It was a captured monkey, disguised as Sita by Ravana's order.
chat.meaning: Vibhishana saw through it: Ravana would never let Sita die. It was an illusion to buy Indrajit time for his rite at Nikumbhila.

Nikumbhila.meaning: a sacred grove and shrine where Indrajit makes his fire offering

Indrajit.meaning: Ravana's son, master of illusion in battle

Vibhishana.meaning: Ravana's brother, who sees through the trick

Brahma.meaning: the creator god, whose boon protects Indrajit, with a condition

recall: a king who became a sage
